Multiparametric MRI Prostate | Amsterdam UMC, AMC | 05 January 2025
Clinical workup prompted by a PSA reading of 5.9 ng/mL alongside malignant suspicion.

FINDINGS:
Glandular volume registers at 29.71 mL. T2 sequences highlight a discrete hypointense focus located posteriorly in the mid-gland left peripheral zone, spanning 12 × 9 × 10 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows pronounced restriction, mirrored by dark ADC mapping. Post-contrast dynamics capture rapid, localized enhancement against adjacent tissue. Extraprostatic spread and seminal vesicle involvement are absent. Pelvic nodal basins appear normal.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left peripheral zone.
Prostate volume 29.71 mL; PSAD 0.199 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.84285355.

previous_notes.author: Dr. C. Peters (GP)
previous_notes.text: Laboratory results showed a PSA rise to 4.1 ng/mL in September 2023, following a baseline of 2.8 ng/mL in April 2022. Driven by this trend and mild urinary complaints, clinicians ordered an mpMRI and initiated a urology referral. Tamsulosin remained part of the regimen for symptom management.
